candidates.mechanism: Dendritic target propagation (DTP): distal dendrites encode a mismatch between top-down excitation and learned lateral dendrite-targeting inhibition; local dendritic state gates plasticity and nudges somatic activity to propagate target information through multilayer E/I circuits.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Separate excitatory/inhibitory cell classes, soma/distal dendrite compartments, dendrite-targeting interneurons, Dale-sign constraints, continuous bidirectional signaling, and dendritic-spike-dependent plasticity including BTSP.
candidates.ai_transfer: Cell Reports 2026 trains multilayer biology-constrained recurrent E/I ANNs on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and nonlinear spirals. DTP is reported comparable to backpropagation on the same constrained architecture; BTSP-based updates also work on MNIST; fixed/random or independently learned top-down weights remain viable.
quantitative_evidence: Principal accuracy/error-alignment plots use five independent network instances.

With fixed random top-down weights, bottom-up/top-down alignment angle moves from 45 degrees initially to about 60 degrees while MNIST accuracy remains comparable to the symmetric-weight DTP condition.
BTSP eligibility/instructive interactions span up to about 5 seconds and yield MNIST performance comparable to the simpler dendritic-state rule.
candidates.artifact_status: Author code is public at Milstein-Lab/EIANN, with an archived Zenodo initial code release DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18602556. Repository was still active in August 2026. This is reproducibility support, not independent replication.
scope_limits: Supervised image/spiral tasks rather than autonomous long-horizon learning.
Exact Fashion-MNIST/CIFAR-10 supplementary table values remain unextracted in this worker state.
No independent external replication located.

primary_sources.title: Cellular and subcellular specialization enables biology-constrained deep learning

candidates.mechanism: Sleep Replay Consolidation (SRC): after ordinary task learning, drive spontaneous/noise-based activity and apply local Hebbian-type plasticity offline to restore latent old-task structure and reduce cross-talk.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Inspired by spontaneous sleep replay and local synaptic plasticity; mechanistic analysis indicates sleep updates suppress task-irrelevant cross-talk while recoverable old-task information remains in weights.
candidates.ai_transfer: Nature Communications 2022 on incremental MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CUB-200 and CIFAR-10, plus later same-lab extensions to equilibrium-propagation recurrent networks and delayed single-sleep consolidation.
quantitative_evidence: CUB-200 sequential baseline after two tasks: task1 5%, task2 95%; with SRC: task1 63.2%, task2 45.4%.
CIFAR-10 overall incremental accuracy: 44% with SRC versus 19% without SRC.
Cross-modal MNIST/Fashion-MNIST overall accuracy: 47% sequential baseline to 61% with SRC; joint-training reference about 90%.
iCaRL MNIST K=100: 65.5% to 78.1% with SRC; K=200: 76.9% to 84.5%.
2025 same-lab MRNN-EP extension: CIFAR-10 sequential 33.56% to 81.30% with SRC, versus 91.87% parallel-training reference; however features were extracted by a pretrained VGG-style network.

2026 delayed-consolidation preprint: after five sequential MNIST tasks, one terminal SRC phase partially recovered all tasks; one reported order had per-task post-SRC accuracies 0.53/0.39/0.67/0.75/0.33 (mean about 0.53), showing recoverability but incomplete restoration.
scope_limits: Original CIFAR-10 and CUB-200 experiments used pre-extracted/frozen visual features rather than end-to-end plastic convolutional stacks.
Sleep phase computational cost was comparable to training an additional task in the studied batching setup.
OWM slightly surpassed SRC on most no-old-data class-incremental tasks in the original paper; SRC is strongest as complementary offline recovery.
The 2025 recurrent extension uses pretrained feature extractors for CIFAR-10 and ResNet-152 ImageNet features for an ImageNet subset, so it is not end-to-end continual visual learning.
The 2025-2026 extensions share authors/lab lineage with SRC and therefore are not independent replication.

candidates.mechanism: Brain-Inspired Replay (BI-R): replay internal/hidden representations generated through context-modulated feedback rather than reconstructing raw sensory inputs; combine conditional replay, context gating, replay-through-feedback and distillation.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Motivated by hippocampal/cortical reactivation and the idea that internally generated memory need not recreate retinal-level inputs.
candidates.ai_transfer: Nature Communications 2020 demonstrated no-data-storage continual learning on 100 permuted-MNIST tasks and split CIFAR-100, including class-incremental evaluation.
quantitative_evidence: Class-IL CIFAR-100, BI-R+SI: 0.344 +/- 0.002 average accuracy with replay-through-feedback versus 0.334 +/- 0.002 when ablated.
100-task permuted MNIST, BI-R+SI: 0.904 +/- 0.005 versus 0.892 +/- 0.004 without replay-through-feedback.
Ablations indicate internal replay is the largest single contributor on CIFAR-100; difficult settings require the combination of components.
scope_limits: CIFAR-100 convolutional layers were pretrained on CIFAR-10 and frozen; replay occurred in later fully connected layers.
Class-IL performance remained substantially below joint training.
No clear independent replication located in this pass.

primary_sources.title: Brain-inspired replay for continual learning with artificial neural networks

candidates.mechanism: Context-dependent gating (XdG): activate sparse, mostly non-overlapping unit populations per task/context, reducing representational interference; combine with synaptic stabilization.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Abstracts context-specific sparse neuronal ensembles into task-conditioned subnetworks.
candidates.ai_transfer: PNAS 2018 tested feedforward and recurrent networks across supervised and reinforcement-learning task sequences.
quantitative_evidence: 100 sequential permuted-MNIST tasks: first-task accuracy 98.2%; mean across all 100 with XdG+synaptic stabilization 95.4%.
500 sequential permuted-MNIST tasks: XdG+SI 90.7% versus SI alone 54.9%.
Optimal gating in the reported 100-task setting was about 80-86.7% of units gated.
scope_limits: Canonical XdG requires task/context identity to choose the gate.
The strong permuted-MNIST setting has unusually separable contexts and may overstate transfer to natural nonstationarity.

primary_sources.title: Alleviating catastrophic forgetting using context-dependent gating and synaptic stabilization

candidates.mechanism: Learned Context-Dependent Gating (LXDG): a gating network maps task inputs directly to sparse hidden-unit gates, with losses encouraging approximately 20% activity, stability on old inputs, and low overlap for new tasks. Gates are recalled from inputs rather than an externally supplied task label.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Motivated by biological recruitment of partially distinct neuronal ensembles for different memories/contexts and by the observation that similar contexts can share ensemble overlap.
candidates.ai_transfer: ICLR 2023 feedforward continual-learning experiments on 50-task permuted MNIST and 50-task rotated MNIST. LXDG removes XdG's explicit test-time task-label requirement and learns context-dependent subnetworks from inputs.
quantitative_evidence: 50-task permuted MNIST final mean accuracy: LXDG+EWC 96%, XDG+EWC 97%, EWC alone 72 +/- 1% SD.
Runs used three random seeds for EWC and LXDG+EWC; after an early first-task instability, LXDG performance stayed stable after about five tasks.
Compared against active dendrites+SI using values copied from that paper: LXDG+EWC 96.0% versus active dendrites+SI 94.4%; authors explicitly warn this comparison was not reproduced by them.
On rotated MNIST, learned gate embeddings formed a ring ordered by rotation angle, so similar task inputs induced similar gates rather than forced orthogonal masks.
scope_limits: Although no explicit task label is needed at test time, training the change/keep losses requires stored unlabeled input batches from prior tasks, so this is not old-data-free continual learning.
Backpropagation and EWC remain central; the neuronal-ensemble mapping is an abstraction rather than a fully local biological learning rule.
Evidence is limited to MNIST-derived benchmarks; RL and natural-image continual learning were future work.
No independent replication located.

primary_sources.title: Artificial Neuronal Ensembles with Learned Context Dependent Gating

candidates.mechanism: Dendritic Localized Learning (DLL): pyramidal-neuron-inspired local forward/backward dynamics with trainable local feedback variables, intended to avoid weight symmetry, global error dependence and a separate global two-phase training protocol.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Inspired by dendritic dynamics/plasticity rather than a direct replication of one isolated biological experiment.
candidates.ai_transfer: ICML 2025 across MLP, CNN and RNN architectures with public code.
quantitative_evidence: CNN average accuracy across MNIST/Fashion-MNIST/SVHN/CIFAR-10: DLL 86.61%, Hebbian 57.43%, R-STDP 62.29%, Forward-Forward 10.67%, Equilibrium Propagation 18.50%, backpropagation 90.67% under reported setups.
CIFAR-10: DLL 70.89% +/- 0.58% versus backpropagation 75.10% +/- 0.54%.
SVHN: DLL 85.81% +/- 0.17% versus backpropagation 95.35% +/- 1.53%.
Electricity forecasting MSE/MAE 0.172/0.321 versus backprop 0.175/0.324; character prediction 33.7% versus backprop 51.9%.
scope_limits: Algorithmic biological-plausibility benchmark rather than continual-learning evidence.
Sequential character prediction remains substantially below backpropagation.
No independent replication located.

corroborating_or_deferred_evidence.lead: Independent 2026 preprint: Sleep-Mediated Replay Prevents Catastrophic Forgetting in Spiking Neural Networks Trained on Sequential Tasks
corroborating_or_deferred_evidence.assessment: Independent authors report Task-A retention 0.206 after sleep versus 0.011 after sequential Task-B without sleep, from 0.589 pre-B. This corroborates sleep/replay broadly but uses replay of prior-task patterns and only two MNIST-derived tasks; it is not a replication of the exact no-old-data SRC mechanism and is not peer-reviewed.

Biophysically detailed hippocampal-thalamocortical slow-wave model interleaving familiar and novel traces. Strong mechanistic neuroscience relevance, but currently deferred because its transfer is primarily a computational brain model rather than a benchmarked general-purpose AI method.

corroborating_or_deferred_evidence.lead: General neuroscience reviews of replay/contextual inference without demonstrated artificial-learning transfer
corroborating_or_deferred_evidence.assessment: Background only; fails this worker's transfer-evidence threshold.
Promising but retain a context-vector mechanism and remain strongest on MNIST-derived benchmarks; natural-image/latent-context evidence remains a frontier.
